name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH16_STMT2_Q01 - Heterodont dentition and human dental formula

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully:

Statement I: An adult human has heterodont dentition consisting of incisors, canines, premolars, and molars.

Statement II: The arrangement of teeth in each half of the upper and lower jaw is represented by the dental formula \(\frac{2123}{2123}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Adult human dentition is characterised by four morphologically distinct types of teeth arranged symmetrically in the upper and lower jaws.

Step 2: Evaluation of Both Claims
The claim that an adult human has heterodont dentition with incisors (I), canines (C), premolars (PM), and molars (M) is correct, as there are 32 permanent teeth of these four types. The claim that the arrangement of teeth in each half of the upper and lower jaw in the order I, C, PM, M is \(\frac{2123}{2123}\) is also correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH16_STMT2_Q02 - Attachment and papillae of human tongue

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully:

Statement I: The tongue is attached to the roof of the oral cavity by a cartilaginous flap called the epiglottis.

Statement II: All papillae present on the upper surface of the tongue are devoid of taste buds.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The tongue is a freely movable muscular organ located on the floor of the oral cavity, whereas the epiglottis is a cartilaginous flap associated with the pharynx and glottis.

Step 2: Evaluation of Both Claims
The claim that the tongue is attached to the roof of the oral cavity by the epiglottis is incorrect; the tongue is attached to the floor of the oral cavity by the frenulum, while the epiglottis prevents food from entering the glottis during swallowing. The claim that all papillae on the upper surface of the tongue lack taste buds is also incorrect, because some of the papillae bear taste buds.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH16_STMT2_Q03 - Pharynx passage and oesophageal opening into stomach

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully:

Statement I: The pharynx serves as a common passage for both food and air.

Statement II: The oesophagus opens directly into the pyloric portion of the stomach.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The oral cavity leads into the pharynx, which connects to both the trachea and the oesophagus, and the oesophagus subsequently leads into the stomach.

Step 2: Evaluation of Both Claims
The claim that the pharynx serves as a common passage for food and air is correct. However, the claim that the oesophagus opens into the pyloric portion of the stomach is incorrect; the oesophagus opens into the cardiac portion of the stomach, whereas the pyloric portion opens into the duodenum.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is correct, whereas the second statement is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH16_STMT2_Q04 - Serosa and sub-mucosa of alimentary canal

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully:

Statement I: Serosa is the innermost layer lining the lumen of the alimentary canal.

Statement II: The sub-mucosal layer is formed of loose connective tissues containing nerves, blood, and lymph vessels.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The wall of the alimentary canal from oesophagus to rectum possesses four concentric layers: serosa, muscularis, sub-mucosa, and mucosa.

Step 2: Evaluation of Both Claims
The claim that serosa is the innermost layer lining the lumen is incorrect; serosa is the outermost layer (made of thin mesothelium with some connective tissues), while mucosa is the innermost layer lining the lumen. The claim that the sub-mucosal layer consists of loose connective tissues containing nerves, blood, and lymph vessels is correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, whereas the second statement is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH16_STMT2_Q05 - Lacteals in villi and goblet cells in mucosa

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully:

Statement I: Intestinal villi are supplied with a network of capillaries and a large lymph vessel called the lacteal.

Statement II: The mucosal epithelium contains goblet cells that secrete mucus to help in lubrication.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The intestinal mucosa is specialised for both nutrient absorption and protective lubrication.

Step 2: Evaluation of Both Claims
The claim that villi are supplied with a network of capillaries and a large lymph vessel called the lacteal is correct. The claim that the mucosal epithelium has goblet cells secreting mucus for lubrication is also correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH16_STMT2_Q06 - Liver size and site of bile synthesis

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully:

Statement I: The liver is the second largest gland of the human body, weighing about 0.2 to 0.5 kg in an adult.

Statement II: Bile is synthesised and secreted by the cells of the gall bladder.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The liver and gall bladder have distinct anatomical and physiological roles in bile production and storage.

Step 2: Evaluation of Both Claims
The claim regarding liver size and weight is incorrect because the liver is the largest gland of the body, weighing about 1.2 to 1.5 kg in an adult human. The claim that bile is synthesised by the gall bladder is also incorrect because bile is secreted by the hepatic cells of the liver and is only stored and concentrated in the gall bladder.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH16_STMT2_Q07 - Compound nature and secretions of pancreas

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully:

Statement I: The pancreas is a compound (both exocrine and endocrine) elongated organ situated between the limbs of the C-shaped duodenum.

Statement II: The exocrine portion of the pancreas secretes the hormones insulin and glucagon.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The pancreas functions as a mixed (compound) gland with separate exocrine and endocrine compartments.

Step 2: Evaluation of Both Claims
The claim that the pancreas is a compound elongated organ situated between the limbs of the C-shaped duodenum is correct. However, the claim that its exocrine portion secretes insulin and glucagon is incorrect; the endocrine portion secretes insulin and glucagon, whereas the exocrine portion secretes an alkaline pancreatic juice containing digestive enzymes.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is correct, whereas the second statement is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH16_STMT2_Q08 - Salivary amylase activity and lysozyme function

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully:

Statement I: Salivary amylase hydrolyses about 70 per cent of starch into maltose in the oral cavity at an optimum pH of 1.8.

Statement II: Lysozyme present in saliva acts as an antibacterial agent that prevents infections.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Saliva contains salivary amylase for partial carbohydrate digestion and lysozyme for antimicrobial defence in the oral cavity.

Step 2: Evaluation of Both Claims
The claim about salivary amylase is incorrect because salivary amylase hydrolyses only about 30 per cent of starch into maltose, and its optimum pH is 6.8 (not 1.8, which is the gastric pH for pepsin). The claim that lysozyme in saliva acts as an antibacterial agent preventing infections is correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, whereas the second statement is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH16_STMT2_Q10 - Activation of trypsinogen and role of bile salts

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully:

Statement I: Trypsinogen in pancreatic juice is activated into active trypsin by hydrochloric acid in the stomach.

Statement II: Bile salts enzymatically convert proteins into proteoses and peptones in the duodenum.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Proenzyme activation and enzymatic protein hydrolysis occur in specific regions of the digestive tract via dedicated enzymes.

Step 2: Evaluation of Both Claims
The claim that trypsinogen is activated by HCl in the stomach is incorrect; trypsinogen is secreted into the duodenum and activated into trypsin by enterokinase secreted by the intestinal mucosa (whereas HCl activates pepsinogen in the stomach). The claim that bile salts enzymatically convert proteins into proteoses and peptones is also incorrect; bile contains no enzymes and functions in fat emulsification and lipase activation, while pepsin converts proteins into proteoses and peptones in the stomach.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH16_STMT2_Q11 - Final digestion by succus entericus and sucrase

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully:

Statement I: The enzymes in succus entericus act on the end products of pancreatic digestion to form simple absorbable forms.

Statement II: Sucrase hydrolyses sucrose into two molecules of glucose.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Succus entericus (intestinal juice) completes the final steps of digestion close to the mucosal epithelial cells.

Step 2: Evaluation of Both Claims
The claim that enzymes in succus entericus act on the end products of pancreatic reactions to form simple absorbable forms is correct. However, the claim that sucrase hydrolyses sucrose into two molecules of glucose is incorrect; sucrase hydrolyses sucrose into glucose and fructose (whereas maltase hydrolyses maltose into two molecules of glucose).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is correct, whereas the second statement is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH16_STMT2_Q12 - Sites of breakdown, absorption, and large intestine role

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully:

Statement I: The breakdown of biomacromolecules occurs primarily in the ileum, while the simple substances formed are absorbed in the duodenum.

Statement II: No significant digestive activity occurs in the large intestine, which absorbs some water, minerals, and certain drugs.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The small and large intestines exhibit clear regional division of labour for digestion, nutrient absorption, and water recovery.

Step 2: Evaluation of Both Claims
The claim that biomacromolecule breakdown occurs in the ileum and absorption occurs in the duodenum is incorrect because the reverse is true: breakdown of biomacromolecules occurs in the duodenum region, and the simple substances formed are absorbed in the jejunum and ileum regions. The claim that no significant digestive activity occurs in the large intestine and that it absorbs some water, minerals, and certain drugs is correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, whereas the second statement is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH16_STMT2_Q13 - Micelles, chylomicrons, and lacteals in fat absorption

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully:

Statement I: Fatty acids and glycerol are first incorporated into small droplets called micelles, which move into the intestinal mucosa.

Statement II: Inside the intestinal mucosa, they are re-formed into protein-coated chylomicrons and transported into lacteals, which ultimately release them into the bloodstream.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Water-insoluble lipid digestion products require micellar solubilisation for mucosal entry and chylomicron packaging for lymphatic transport.

Step 2: Evaluation of Both Claims
The claim that fatty acids and glycerol are incorporated into micelles to move into the intestinal mucosa is correct. The claim that they are re-formed into small protein-coated fat globules called chylomicrons and transported into lacteals, which ultimately release the absorbed substances into the bloodstream, is also correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH16_STMT2_Q14 - Mechanisms of water and electrolyte absorption

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully:

Statement I: Transport of water across the intestinal mucosa occurs by active transport against the osmotic gradient.

Statement II: Small amounts of glucose and chloride ions are absorbed into the lacteals exclusively by active transport.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Water and small water-soluble solutes cross the intestinal mucosa into the blood via passive gradients, facilitated carriers, or active pumps.

Step 2: Evaluation of Both Claims
The claim that water is transported by active transport against the osmotic gradient is incorrect; transport of water depends upon the osmotic gradient. The claim that small amounts of glucose and chloride ions are absorbed into lacteals exclusively by active transport is also incorrect; small amounts of glucose, amino acids, and electrolytes like chloride ions are generally absorbed into the blood by simple diffusion depending upon concentration gradients.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH16_STMT2_Q15 - Vomiting reflex and definition of constipation

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully:

Statement I: Vomiting is a reflex action controlled by the vomit centre in the medulla and is preceded by a feeling of nausea.

Statement II: In constipation, bowel movements occur at an abnormally high frequency with increased liquidity of the faecal discharge.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Digestive disorders include neural reflex disturbances like vomiting and motility disorders like constipation and diarrhoea.

Step 2: Evaluation of Both Claims
The claim that vomiting is controlled by the vomit centre in the medulla and is preceded by nausea is correct. However, the claim describing constipation as frequent liquid bowel movements is incorrect; abnormal frequency of bowel movement and increased liquidity of faecal discharge define diarrhoea, whereas in constipation faeces are retained within the colon as bowel movements occur irregularly.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is correct, whereas the second statement is incorrect.

Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH16_STMT2_Q16 - Etiology and clinical features of Marasmus and Kwashiorkor

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully:

Statement I: Marasmus is produced by protein deficiency unaccompanied by calorie deficiency in children more than one year in age.

Statement II: Unlike Marasmus, Kwashiorkor shows some fat left under the skin along with extensive oedema and swelling of body parts.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Protein-energy malnutrition (PEM) causes Marasmus and Kwashiorkor, which differ in caloric sufficiency, typical age of onset, and presence of oedema and subcutaneous fat.

Step 2: Evaluation of Both Claims
The claim that Marasmus is caused by protein deficiency without calorie deficiency in children over one year old is incorrect; that describes Kwashiorkor, whereas Marasmus is caused by a simultaneous deficiency of proteins and calories in infants less than a year in age. The claim that, unlike Marasmus, Kwashiorkor retains some fat under the skin and exhibits extensive oedema and swelling of body parts is correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, whereas the second statement is correct.
